arxiv-1911-04970.creator: Kürşat Tekbıyık 1 2 , Ali Rıza Ekti 1 4 , Ali Görçin 1 5 , Güneş Karabulut Kurt 2 , Cihat Keçeci 1 3
arxiv-1911-04970.description: Abstract AMC ( AMC ) has been studied for more than a quarter of a century; however, it has been difficult to design a classifier that operates successfully under changing multipath fading conditions and other impairments. Recently, DL ( DL )–based methods are adopted by AMC systems and major improvements are reported.

arxiv-2105-04572.title: Stringent axion constraints with Event Horizon Telescope polarimetric measurements of M87 ⋆
arxiv-2105-04572.creator: Yifan Chen 1, Yuxin Liu 2, Ru-Sen Lu 3,4,5, Yosuke Mizuno 6,7, Jing Shu 1,8,9,10,11,12, Xiao Xue 1,8, Qiang Yuan 13,14,10, Yue Zhao 15
arxiv-2105-04572.description: Abstract The hitherto unprecedented angular resolution of the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has created exciting opportunities in the search for new physics. Recently, the linear polarization of radiation emitted near the supermassive black hole M87 ⋆ was measured on four separate days, precisely enabling tests of the existence of a dense axion cloud produced by a spinning black hole.

arxiv-2302-07792.title: Generation, dynamics, and correlations of the fission fragments’ angular momenta
arxiv-2302-07792.creator: Guillaume Scamps 1, George Bertsch 2
arxiv-2302-07792.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guillaume Scamps 1, George Bertsch 2. The generation of angular momentum in fissioning nuclei is not well understood. The predictions of different models disagree, particularly concerning the correlation between the fragments’ angular momenta. In this article, a time-dependent collective Hamiltonian model is proposed to treat the generation of the angular momentum in the fission fragments due to the quantum uncertainty principle as well as the dynamics of the collective wave function during and after scission.

arxiv-2307-02798.title: Semi-supervised Domain Adaptive Medical Image Segmentation through Consistency Regularized Disentangled Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2307-02798.creator: Hritam Basak, Zhaozheng Yin
arxiv-2307-02798.description: Abstract Although unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is a promising direction to alleviate domain shift, they fall short of their supervised counterparts. In this work, we investigate relatively less explored semi-supervised domain adaptation (SSDA) for medical image segmentation, where access to a few labeled target samples can improve the adaptation performance substantially. Specifically, we propose a two-stage training process.

arxiv-2405-18532.title: Automatic Forward Model Parameterization with Bayesian Inference of Conformational Populations
arxiv-2405-18532.creator: Robert M. Raddi, Tim Marshall, Vincent A. Voelz
arxiv-2405-18532.description: Abstract To quantify how well theoretical predictions of structural ensembles agree with experimental measurements, we depend on the accuracy of forward models. These models are computational frameworks that generate observable quantities from molecular configurations based on empirical relationships linking specific molecular properties to experimental measurements.

arxiv-2504-05152.title: PanoDreamer: Consistent Text to 360-Degree Scene Generation
arxiv-2504-05152.creator: Zhexiao Xiong, Zhang Chen, Zhong Li, Nathan Jacobs, [0.5ex] OPPO US Research Center
arxiv-2504-05152.description: Abstract Automatically generating a complete 3D scene from a text description, a reference image, or both has significant applications in fields like virtual reality and gaming. However, current methods often generate low-quality textures and inconsistent 3D structures. This is especially true when extrapolating significantly beyond the field of view of the reference image.

arxiv-2505-23904.title: Cosmology with Topological Deep Learning
arxiv-2505-23904.creator: Jun-Young Lee, Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro
arxiv-2505-23904.description: Abstract The standard cosmological model with cold dark matter posits a hierarchical formation of structures. We introduce topological neural networks (TNNs), implemented as message-passing neural networks on higher-order structures, to effectively capture the topological information inherent in these hierarchies that traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) fail to account for.

pmc-10648840.creator: Luís Manuel Cunha Batalha, Josefa Palop-Muñoz, Carlos Alberto Cruz de Oliveira, Carlos Saus-Ortega, Paulo Alexandre Carvalho Ferreira, María-Rosario Gómez-Romero, Nicola Magnavita
pmc-10648840.description: The cultivation of critical thinking and decision-making skills promotes student autonomy. Only a few instruments measure nursing students’ autonomy, and the PALOP® Scale is one of them. This study aimed to semantically and culturally adapt the PALOP® Scale to European Portuguese and assess the psychometric properties of a short version.

pmc-10675145.title: Tailoring Risperidone-Loaded Glycethosomal In Situ Gels Using Box–Behnken Design for Treatment of Schizophrenia-Induced Rats via Intranasal Route
pmc-10675145.creator: Marwa H. Abdallah, Hemat El-Sayed El-Horany, Hanan M. El-Nahas, Tarek M. Ibrahim
pmc-10675145.description: Schizophrenic patients often face challenges with adherence to oral regimens. The study aimed to highlight the potentiality of intranasal ethanol/glycerin-containing lipid-nanovesicles (glycethosomes) incorporated into in situ gels for sustaining anti-psychotic risperidone (RS) release. The Box–Behnken Design (BBD) was followed for in vitro characterization. Glycethosomal-based in situ gels were examined by physical, ex vivo, and in vivo investigations.

pmc-11281987.title: High throughput spatial immune mapping reveals an innate immune scar in post-COVID-19 brains
pmc-11281987.creator: Marius Schwabenland, Dilara Hasavci, Sibylle Frase, Katharina Wolf, Nikolaus Deigendesch, Joerg M. Buescher, Kirsten D. Mertz, Benjamin Ondruschka, Hermann Altmeppen, Jakob Matschke, Markus Glatzel, Stephan Frank, Robert Thimme, Juergen Beck, Jonas A. Hosp, Thomas Blank, Bertram Bengsch, Marco Prinz
pmc-11281987.description: The underlying pathogenesis of neurological sequelae in post-COVID-19 patients remains unclear. Here, we used multidimensional spatial immune phenotyping and machine learning methods on brains from initial COVID-19 survivors to identify the biological correlate associated with previous SARS-CoV-2 challenge. Compared to healthy controls, individuals with post-COVID-19 revealed a high percentage of TMEM119+P2RY12+CD68+Iba1+HLA-DR+CD11c+SCAMP2+ microglia assembled in prototypical cellular nodules.

pmc-11713820.description: BackgroundHistopathological analysis of autopsied brains is the gold standard of diagnosis in neurodegenerative disorders. Co‐registered histology and MRI scans aid in understanding pathology and structural features. Previous studies focused on the medial temporal lobe (MTL) for atrophy patterns in phosphorylated tau (p‐tau) pathology and in whole hemisphere scans with contralateral semi‐quantitative p‐tau measures.

pmc-12551113.title: Effects of Elastic Band Training on Physical Performance in Team Sports: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12551113.creator: Dušan Stanković, Anja Lazić, Nebojša Trajković, Miladin Okičić, Aleksa Bubanj, Tomáš Vencúrik, Tomislav Gašić, Saša Bubanj, Athanasios Tsoukos
pmc-12551113.description: Objectives: Elastic band training is a popular alternative to traditional resistance methods, but its effects on sport-specific performance in team athletes remain inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the efficacy of elastic band training on muscular strength, linear sprint, change of direction (COD), and jump height in team sport athletes.

pmc-13406641.title: Immunotherapy and Relevant Antibody–Drug Conjugates in Gynecologic Oncology: Recent Advances, Ongoing Challenges, and Future Directions
pmc-13406641.creator: Ting-Tai Yen, Tina Yi-Jin Hsieh, Eugene P. Toy
pmc-13406641.description: Simple SummaryGynecologic cancers, including endometrial, cervical, and ovarian cancers, remain major causes of illness and death worldwide. New treatments are changing how these cancers are managed. Immune checkpoint inhibitors help the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells, while antibody–drug conjugates deliver cancer-killing drugs more directly to tumor cells.

pmc-13439452.title: A narrow developmental window defines PKN2’s essential role in ventricular chamber morphogenesis
pmc-13439452.creator: Julijus Bogomolovas, Zengming Zhang, Christa Trexler, Alex Campos, Jennifer Veevers, Zeyu Chen, Ju Chen
pmc-13439452.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Protein kinase N2 (PKN2) is essential for embryonic heart development, but the precise timing and cellular requirement in cardiomyocytes are not well understood. Here we show that, in a constitutive cardiomyocyte-specific knockout (cKO) of PKN2, we observe partially penetrant early postnatal lethality, non-progressive systolic dysfunction in survivors, and a distinctive “coin-pouch” ventricular geometry resembling the embryonic shape, linking the phenotype to a developmental origin rather than ongoing pathology.

pmc-13543025.title: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (MRONJ) Prevention
pmc-13543025.creator: Nasimeh Baghalipour, Omid Moztarzadeh, Bacem Othman, Yasmin Dehghani, Lukas Hauer
pmc-13543025.description: PurposeMedication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious complication that can arise in patients receiving antiresorptive or antiangiogenic therapy. Despite known predisposing factors, effective prophylaxis is currently little used. We therefore sought to assess the standardised prevention protocols that are used in our institution for reducing MRONJs among at-risk patients and to quantify the consistency of the effects.
